clue.text: Sign of injury? Dab lotions freely

indicators.note: used freely, the letters of the two words are let loose into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone dabbing lotion liberally on a wound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freely' looks like it describes how the lotions are dabbed on, but it is the anagram signal on DABLOTIONS.
explanation.definitionFit: A mark of dried blood on cloth or skin is evidence that somebody was hurt, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Former President to show embarrassment, getting left out

indicators.note: being omitted signals that a letter is removed from the word for the embarrassment
with 'getting' before it, 'out' says a letter is excluded from the word for the embarrassment

parts.note: to blush is to go red with embarrassment

explanation.surface: An ex-president turns red after being excluded from something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' plays a double role in the surface (excluded), but here it supplies L, which is dropped from BLUSH.
explanation.definitionFit: Two US presidents, father and son, bore this surname, so either is a former holder of the office.

clue.text: What may have lost its flavour for sailor?

definitions.text: What may have lost its flavour
definitions.meaning: seasoning that has gone stale over time, taken literally as aged seasoning
a veteran seaman with long experience

explanation.surface: A riddle asking what stale seasoning might be good for.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the phrase is stale table seasoning; as an idiom, it is a weathered seafarer.
explanation.definitionFit: An experienced seaman is called this idiomatically, while literally the words describe aged seasoning that has lost its taste.

clue.text: A direction is given about books crossword setters may use

indicators.note: letters given a turn about are shuffled into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction on which reference works compilers should consult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given about' shuffles the twelve letters of A DIRECTION IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Reference books listing words and meanings are standard tools for compilers checking their vocabulary.

clue.text: Most of the water sport is confusing

indicators.note: most of a word means all of it except its final letter

parts.note: rowing is a sport practised on rivers and lakes

explanation.surface: A puzzled remark that a certain aquatic pastime is baffling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'water sport is confusing' reads as one complaint, but 'is' only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw someone is to disconcert or bewilder them, so the participle is a synonym of baffling.

clue.text: Institute entertains Her Majesty in an enclosure

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to hold them within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: An institution hosts the monarch inside a fenced-off area.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is crossword shorthand for the late Queen (Elizabeth Regina).
explanation.definitionFit: Something placed inside a letter or magazine, such as a leaflet, is an enclosure.

clue.text: Sword keeper has knocked over

indicators.note: something knocked over is upended, so in a light the letters run the other way
the word keeper has the required letters within it

explanation.surface: A goalkeeper or wicketkeeper toppled a blade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' marks EEPE sitting inside KEEPER; 'knocked over' then turns it around.
explanation.definitionFit: A fencing weapon with a stiff blade, used in one of the three Olympic fencing disciplines.

clue.text: Artist, one getting tied up?

definitions.meaning: someone who makes pictures with brush and colours
a rope at a boat's bow used to tie it to a quay or post

explanation.surface: An artist who is being bound, or is very busy.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is nautical: the rope fixed to a small boat's bow for mooring it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a person who works in oils or watercolours and the mooring line on a dinghy.

clue.text: Niece working under specialist briefly accumulated skill

indicators.note: in a down light, what is under comes after
a word said briefly is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: an expert is a specialist

indicators.note: letters set working are moved around into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A young relative at work under a short-spoken expert builds up know-how.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' looks like the niece's job, but it signals the anagram; 'under' places it below in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Knowledge and ability built up over time through practice is what the word describes.

clue.text: Naughty lady, only half educated, in state of anxiety

indicators.note: one piece sits in the middle of the other

parts.note: stress is a state of worry and anxiety

indicators.note: only half of a word means its first half of letters

explanation.surface: A poorly schooled mischievous woman is fretting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Naughty' appears to be anagram signal, but it is part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who sets out to entice and lead someone astray is a temptress, playfully called naughty.

clue.text: Small thin person is quietly hiding behind wife

indicators.note: what hides behind something comes after it, so these letters follow

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for wife in genealogies
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A meek person cowers silently behind his spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A slight, slender figure, like a wisp of smoke, can be described with this word.

clue.text: Presumed quality of archdeacon, never going wrong, having competence

indicators.note: letters going wrong are knocked out of their order

parts.note: ability means competence

explanation.surface: A churchman's assumed virtues: never erring and being capable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going wrong' turns NEVER into VENER. An archdeacon in the Church of England is formally styled 'the Venerable'.
explanation.definitionFit: Archdeacons bear the title 'the Venerable', so being worthy of reverence is assumed of them by their style.

clue.text: Garment beginning to smell, not completely dry

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter
a word not completely given loses its last letter

parts.note: arid means dry

explanation.surface: Clothing that starts to whiff because it was not fully dried.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to' takes S from SMELL; 'not completely' trims ARID to ARI.
explanation.definitionFit: A long draped length of cloth worn by women in South Asia is a traditional item of dress.

clue.text: English bird returning, back briefly in the city

indicators.note: returning means these words are read in the other direction

parts.note: a crow is a black bird

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: An English bird flies back to town after a short stay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns ECROW into WORCE; 'briefly' trims STERN to STER.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathedral city in the West Midlands of England, home of the famous sauce.

clue.text: Twenty directors that may be seen at Lord's

definitions.text: that may be seen at Lord's

parts.note: a score is twenty
a board is a company's body of directors

explanation.surface: Twenty company executives turn up at a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is the famous London cricket ground, which has a large display of runs and wickets.
explanation.definitionFit: A large display showing runs and wickets is a feature of any cricket ground, including Lord's.

clue.text: Not the only one that letter deals with?

definitions.text: Not the only one that letter deals with?

parts.words: Not the only one that letter deals with?
parts.note: a 'letter' here is a landlord who lets property, and this is one of two or more people sharing a lease

explanation.surface: A puzzle about someone who is not the sole recipient of a piece of mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' suggests correspondence, but it means one who lets a property.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone holding a lease jointly with another is one of several renters a landlord deals with.

clue.text: Member in river? I'm concerned!

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the other

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
an arm is a limb, or member, of the body

explanation.surface: Someone panics on seeing a limb in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee flows through Wales and England (another runs in Scotland).
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of mild worry or dismay, equivalent to 'oh dear'.

clue.text: Understand what can fool people, right?

parts.note: cons are tricks or swindles that dupe people
true means right or correct

explanation.surface: A question about grasping what tricks people, seeking confirmation.
explanation.definitionFit: To interpret or take a meaning from words is to understand them in a given way.

clue.text: Agent gets nothing right in official document

parts.note: a rep, short for representative, is a sales agent
O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A sales agent gets everything correct in a formal paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal written account of findings, as issued by a committee, is an official paper.

clue.text: Man is put into part — player on stage?

indicators.note: these letters are put into the middle of the other piece

parts.note: Ian is a man's name

explanation.surface: An actor is cast in a role, as a player in a theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'player on stage' suggests an actor, but it is a musician at a recital.
explanation.definitionFit: A keyboard musician performing at a concert plays on a stage, giving the playful question mark.

clue.text: Like a man kept in order

definitions.text: Like a man kept in order

parts.words: Like a man kept in order
parts.note: the 'order' is a religious order, and the man kept within it is a monk

explanation.surface: Describing a disciplined man under control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept in order' suggests discipline, but the order is a religious community.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to monks living under religious vows in a cloistered community.

clue.text: Adolescent could be free agent, putting father off

indicators.note: what the letters could be once rearranged, after the father's letters are put off

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title

explanation.surface: A youngster could go independent once Dad is out of the picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting father off' removes FR from FREE AGENT; 'could be' rearranges what is left, EEAGENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the years thirteen to nineteen, as in an adolescent's moods.

clue.text: Draw back, as soldiers getting cold, needing fuel

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a British Army corps of soldiers
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
oil is a fuel

explanation.surface: Troops retreat when chilled and in need of fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: To flinch or spring back in fear or disgust is to pull away sharply.

clue.text: Celeb's art may be seen in these ornamental pieces

indicators.note: the letters of the two words may be seen rearranged in the solution

explanation.surface: A celebrity's artistry shows in their decorative jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be seen in these' shuffles CELEBSART.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorative bands or chains worn on the wrist are ornamental items of jewellery.

clue.text: Animal that is getting cross — head of beast must be held

indicators.note: the letter must be held inside the other piece

parts.note: ie, id est, means that is

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: An angry creature has to be restrained by the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of' takes B from BEAST, held inside IE; 'cross' looks like anger but is X.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild mountain goat with long curved horns, found in the Alps.

clue.text: Defeated? No feat or achievement

indicators.note: 'no feat' says those letters are not in the first word, so they are removed

explanation.surface: A beaten competitor asks whether nothing was accomplished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' removes FEAT from DEFEATED.
explanation.definitionFit: An act, especially a notable one, is an accomplishment or exploit.

clue.text: Particular Bible translation I had, being keen

parts.note: AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: An enthusiast owned a specific version of scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: AV is the Authorised (King James) Version of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Eager and enthusiastic, as an avid reader is.

clue.text: Bring together a number in the mathematics class?

definitions.meaning: to organise elements so they work together harmoniously

definitions.text: a number in the mathematics class?
definitions.meaning: each of the numbers locating a point on a graph

explanation.surface: Assembling a figure in a maths lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'class' is a pun: not a lesson but the category of numbers that fix a point on axes.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to organise harmoniously; the noun is one of the values giving a position on a graph.

clue.text: Responsibility for tax

definitions.meaning: a levy charged on imports or goods

explanation.surface: Who is liable for paying a levy.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an obligation and a charge on imported goods, as in customs levies.

clue.text: One not totally alert, boss about to retire?

definitions.meaning: a chief who is tired and ready for bed, read literally

explanation.surface: A dozy employee, or a manager nearing retirement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retire' suggests leaving work, but means going to bed; a drowsy chief is read literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A drowsy or half-awake person is affectionately called this; literally a weary boss ready for bed.
